anomalies.description: A sudden, vigorous plume of ash and steam erupts from the volcano's flank, indicating a phreatic or small explosive event; the plume expands rapidly upward and laterally in frames f0–f1 and is still rising in f2.

A volcanic explosion begins at the summit of a mountain, with an initial plume of ash and gas erupting from the crater (visible from f1), rapidly expanding into a large, billowing dark ash cloud that rises and spreads over several seconds (f2–f15). The eruption is sustained and grows in volume, consistent with a major explosive volcanic event.
A large volcanic explosion with a rapidly expanding ash plume and pyroclastic flow descending the flank; the eruption intensifies progressively over the sequence.
